$comment: Throne and Liberty event schedule. Captured from questlog.gg's event calendar on
This is DETERMINISTIC DATA, not a live feed. The calendar renders a fixed weekly grid:
a region selector, a UTC offset, and the same daily time slots repeating. There is no
spawn API to poll — reports are that Amazon never exposed one. So the timer computes
everything locally from this table plus the player's region and timezone, which is more
reliable than any scraper and has no runtime dependency on a third-party site.
Maintenance: this needs a refresh when a patch changes the rotation. It is a data file
edit, not a code change — that is the point of shipping it as JSON.
STATUS: time slots and event types are CONFIRMED from the live calendar. The specific
boss assigned to each Field Boss slot per weekday is NOT yet captured — see
`bossRotation` below. The timer is useful without it (it can say 'Field Bosses in 18
minutes'); naming the boss is a refinement.
$timeBasis: SLOT TIMES ARE UTC, and weekday keys are UTC weekdays. Converted 2026-08-06 from the Pacific
wall-clock times read off the client (PDT, UTC-7).
Why: a world boss spawns at ONE instant for the region, and every player sees that instant in
their own zone. Storing the wall clock made the timer correct only for players whose machine zone
happens to match the server's -- a player on the same Americas server in Eastern time got a
countdown three hours early that looked entirely plausible.
THE WEEKDAY MOVES. 17:00 Pacific Friday is 00:00 UTC SATURDAY, so every evening slot rolls to the
next UTC day and Sunday's siege now sits on Monday. localPst is kept on each slot so this file
stays verifiable against the client without doing the arithmetic in your head.
DST IS UNRESOLVED. Every slot lands on a whole or half UTC hour and 17:00 Pacific is exactly UTC
midnight, which reads as UTC-native and therefore DST-immune -- but that is one capture in one
season. November settles it: if the client still shows 17:00 Pacific after the change, the
schedule is wall-clock and these stored times have drifted an hour; if it shows 16:00, UTC is
right. Check it then rather than rediscovering a one-hour error as a mystery.
$scheduleShape: RESOLVED. This block recorded that a flat dailySlots list could not express the real schedule;
the reshape it asked for is done and the shape below is the result. Kept as provenance for WHY the
structure is what it is, since the flat form looks simpler and is a tempting thing to revert to.

$iconIndex: The map's Content Settings window lists EVERY boss next to its icon WITH ITS NAME IN TEXT —
roughly 38 bosses (most in normal and 'Ascended' form), 9 archbosses including Ramux, and 6
boonstones. That single screen is a complete icon->name index, and capturing it once solves
the schedule's icon problem the same way the named-currency reference solves the currency
bar's. Prompt for it on first run.
Each entry has a checkbox. A boss the player has unticked does not appear on their schedule
at all, so the index doubles as the filter state and both are worth reading.
Consequence: the fieldBosses roster below (seven entries, from getFieldBossEntries) is badly
incomplete and should not be built on.
$regionCoverage: questlog only has real boss data for EUROPE. Confirmed 2026-08-04 by a player of the game,
and consistent with what the calendar renders: Europe shows named T3/T2 pairs per slot,
while Americas shows only generic 'Field Bosses' markers and Asia shows nothing.
So the Americas entries below are NOT a captured boss rotation — they are questlog's generic
event markers. Do not present them as a boss schedule, and do not wait for questlog to fill
in NA or Asia; the data is not there to scrape.
THE REAL SOURCE FOR NA AND ASIA IS THE PLAYER'S OWN CLIENT. The in-game map lists the day's
bosses and spawn times down the left side, per-server accurate by definition, for every
region including the ones no external site covers. That makes it a user-initiated capture —
the same pattern already used for the Combat Power tooltip and the named-currency reference,
and something this app can already do. See docs/boss-timer.md, which reached this conclusion
before the region gap was confirmed.
$timeModel: SUPERSEDED BY $timeBasis ABOVE — this file now stores UTC. Kept because the argument it makes is
the reason DST is still an open question, and deleting it would leave that question unmotivated.
It argued for storing WALL-CLOCK times plus a named timeZone, on the grounds that if the game
schedules by Pacific wall clock then 17:00 Pacific is 00:00 UTC in summer and 01:00 UTC in winter,
so a UTC table would be an hour wrong for half the year and need re-capturing twice annually.
That reasoning is sound and remains unrefuted.
What overrode it was a different error, and a live one rather than a seasonal one: a wall-clock
table was read in the CALLER'S zone, so it was correct only for players whose machine matched the
server. An Eastern player on an Americas server got a countdown three hours early. Being wrong for
some players all the time beats being wrong for all players half the time, and only one of the two
So the trade was made knowingly, and the DST question it turns on is still open — see the November
test recorded in $timeBasis. If the schedule does prove wall-clock anchored, the fix is NOT to
revert this: it is a wall-clock table plus the server's own zone, resolved independently of the
$timezoneWarning: UNRESOLVED, AND IT INVALIDATES EVERY HOUR IN THIS FILE IF WRONG.
questlog's calendar renders a 'UTC -07:00' header, which is the VIEWER'S timezone, not the
server's. So the hour values captured from that page may already be converted into the
capturing machine's local time rather than being server-local wall clock. Both the Americas
and Europe slots here were read off that page from a UTC-07:00 machine.
If they are viewer-local, every entry is offset by the difference between UTC-07:00 and the
player's server timezone — for Europe that is around nine hours, which would make the

$source: TWO STREAMS RUN AT ONCE, and the game splits them across two tabs of the same map panel.
Both are captured from a live client and both are modelled here:
weeklySlots  <- the DAILY tab.  Siege and archbosses. Per weekday, with empty days.
hourlySlots  <- the HOURLY tab. The regular field bosses. EVERY day, composition rotating.
A day with archbosses has both, which is the whole reason the merge exists. Before it, a
weekday the Daily tab leaves empty produced a countdown to something two days out while seven
field bosses were actually spawning that evening.
dailySlots at the bottom is neither: it is the older questlog-derived guess, kept only so the
difference stays visible (questlog claims 19:00/22:00, the client shows 17:00/20:00). It is a
FALLBACK for weeklySlots, never additive. Only hourlySlots stacks.
=== DAILY TAB -> weeklySlots ===
Structure is stable across the captured 21 days: Mon and Thu empty (Pacific), Sun 18:00 castle
siege, Tue/Wed/Fri/Sat carrying 17:00 and 20:00. Slot COMPOSITION rotates -- one boss at 17:00
and five at 20:00 one week, inverted the next -- but the times do not.
TYPED ArchBosses, NOT FieldBosses, corrected 2026-08-06. The Daily tab carries only siege and
archbosses; the regular field bosses are the other stream. Calling these FieldBosses was wrong
on its own terms, and once both streams show at once it also left two identical-looking rows
with no way to tell which one was worth organising for.
SIEGE IS WEEKLY -- 18:00 every Sunday Pacific, same time, corrected 2026-08-06 by the product
owner. An earlier pass read 16/08 Sun as an empty row and concluded biweekly. That was a
misread, and it was published. The everyDays/since machinery it motivated is kept because it is
tested and harmless, but nothing in this file uses it any more.
=== HOURLY TAB -> hourlySlots, read from the client 2026-08-06 ===
Seven slots a day. The list starts at 08:00 with nothing above it and nothing after 23:00, so
in Pacific terms bosses run 11:00 to 23:00 and the rest of the day is genuinely empty:
11:00  2 bosses      peace, rotating
14:00  2 bosses      peace, rotating
18:00  2 bosses      peace, rotating
18:30  1 boss        GUILD PvP
21:00  2 bosses      peace, rotating
21:30  1 boss        GUILD PvP
23:00  2 bosses      peace, rotating
The two guild slots sit at fixed times every day and are the only single-event slots. They
carry "mode": "guild" -- a claim about the SLOT, not about a boss, which is what lets the
countdown say "Guild Boss" without inventing which boss it is. That distinction matters more
than it looks: a player without a guild is locked out entirely, so an unmarked row sends them
across the map twice a day for a contest they cannot enter.
The peace slots rotate randomly through the regular roster (Talus, Excavator-9 and the rest) so
they stay generic Field Bosses. Naming a rotating slot would be wrong most days, and wrong
confidently.
THE NEXT-DAY ROLL ON THESE IS A NO-OP, and it is the one thing here that looks like an error.
18:00 Pacific is 01:00 UTC the FOLLOWING day, so five of the seven appear to have moved. They
have not: the table applies to every UTC day, so the union over all days covers every Pacific
day's seven exactly once. This is why hourlySlots is a flat list with no weekday keys -- unlike
weeklySlots, where the same roll genuinely moves events between named days.
ONE REAL COLLISION, deliberately kept. Sunday 18:00 Pacific is both the weekly siege and an
hourly field-boss slot, so Monday 01:00 UTC yields two spawns at the same instant. They are
different events and collapsing them would hide one behind the other.
=== BOSS NAMES ===
Each slot takes an optional "bosses" array, because ONE slot can hold several bosses at the
same time. With names the overlay reads "20:00 - Ahzreil, Talus, Grand Aelon"; with the array
absent or empty it falls back to the event type, which is true rather than a guess. Never put a
name here that has not been read off the client: a plausible wrong boss sends the player across
the map for nothing.
The names come from the map's Content Settings window, which lists every boss beside its icon
in text. That is a one-time user capture; the schedule icons are unlabelled on their own.
=== ARCHBOSS COMPOSITION, supplied by the product owner 2026-08-06 for 07/08-25/08 ===
Cast is always the same five: Ramux, Ascended Giant Cordy, Ascended Deluzhnoa, Ascended Queen
Bellandir, Ascended Tevent.
STILL NOT NAMED IN THE SLOTS ABOVE, because two things are not derivable from three weeks:
- WHICH boss is guild on a given day. Sequenced by date it runs T, C, D, T, C, R, Q, R, T,
then TWO on 22/08 (D at 17:00 and R at 20:00), then Q. Both the one-per-day rule and any
clean rotation break at 22/08.
- WHETHER Ramux appears. It held to Wed+Sat for three weeks -- absent every Fri and on Tue
11/08 and 18/08 -- then appeared on Tue 25/08.
Three weeks cannot separate a longer cycle from server-side randomisation. So these need DATED
entries refreshed per capture, not weekday ones with a guessed composition. Naming the wrong
contest is worse than naming none: a guildless player told a boss is open, or a guild told it is
theirs, both waste the trip.
$hourlyComment: Written in PACIFIC order with localPst on every row, so this reads top-to-bottom against the
client's own Hourly tab. The parser sorts by UTC time, so file order is presentation only.

Europe.$status: CAPTURED 2026-08-04 from questlog's event calendar. SEE $timezoneWarning — the hour values are NOT yet confirmed to be server-local.
$note: Europe is NOT a copy of Americas, which is why assuming it was would have been wrong:
it runs FIVE boss slots a day (Americas runs two) and pairs a T3 'Ascended' boss with a
T2 boss in every one. Observed names include Ascended Morokai, Ascended Cornelius,
Ascended Adentus and Ascended Chernobog on the T3 side, with Pakilo Naru and Daigon on
the T2 side. Morokai and Pakilo Naru do not appear in the fieldBosses roster below, so
that roster is Americas-shaped and incomplete for Europe.
Per-weekday boss assignment is still NOT captured: the Boss Schedule grid renders each
boss as an image with no alt text, so names only appear on hover.

Asia.$status: NO SOURCE. questlog has no boss data for this region — see $regionCoverage.

fieldBosses.$comment: Roster from eventCalendar.getFieldBossEntries?input={"language":"en"}. Ids are questlog's; names are display names. Species tags are NOT in that payload and matter for advice — a boss's species pairs with the character sheet's Species tab, so 'swap to Demon damage before 21:00' becomes possible. Fill them in when captured.

bossRotation.$status: NOT CAPTURED. Which boss occupies each Field Boss slot on each weekday. Capture by opening each day on questlog's event calendar. Until filled, the timer announces the slot type ('Field Bosses') without naming the boss.

archBosses.$status: NOT CAPTURED. Arch bosses run a separate, less frequent schedule. Ramux arrived in 4.5.0 (Stillreach, two-phase with Atirat). A 'Boosted Arch Bosses' event ran 2026-07-28 to 2026-08-11 with four spawning simultaneously — note that limited-time events perturb the normal rotation, so the timer should support a temporary override rather than assuming the base table always holds.
